question: Top 10 client groups by trailing 12-month revenue
sql:
SELECT g.group_id, g.group_name, g.segment, round(sum(r.revenue_chf), 2) AS revenue_ttm_chf
FROM sandbox.jg_banking_genie.revenue_monthly r JOIN sandbox.jg_banking_genie.client_group g ON g.group_id = r.group_id
WHERE r.month_end > add_months((SELECT max(month_end) FROM sandbox.jg_banking_genie.revenue_monthly), -12)
GROUP BY g.group_id, g.group_name, g.segment
ORDER BY revenue_ttm_chf DESC LIMIT 10

question: Groups using more than 80% of their credit limits
sql:
WITH latest AS (SELECT max(as_of_date) AS d FROM sandbox.jg_banking_genie.credit_facility_monthly)
SELECT g.group_id, g.group_name, g.segment, c.as_of_date,
       sum(c.credit_limit_chf) AS credit_limit_chf, sum(c.drawn_amount_chf) AS drawn_amount_chf,
       round(sum(c.drawn_amount_chf) / sum(c.credit_limit_chf), 4) AS credit_utilisation
FROM sandbox.jg_banking_genie.credit_facility_monthly c
JOIN latest ON c.as_of_date = latest.d
JOIN sandbox.jg_banking_genie.account a ON a.account_id = c.account_id AND a.status = 'Open' AND a.product_category = 'Lending'
JOIN sandbox.jg_banking_genie.client_group g ON g.group_id = c.group_id
GROUP BY g.group_id, g.group_name, g.segment, c.as_of_date
HAVING sum(c.credit_limit_chf) > 0 AND sum(c.drawn_amount_chf) / sum(c.credit_limit_chf) > 0.8
ORDER BY credit_utilisation DESC

question: Top-100 clients by assets not contacted in the last 6 months
sql:
WITH top100 AS (
  SELECT group_id, group_name, segment, as_of_date, assets_at_bank_chf
  FROM sandbox.jg_banking_genie.v_group_net_position ORDER BY assets_at_bank_chf DESC LIMIT 100),
last_contact AS (
  SELECT group_id, max(interaction_date) AS last_interaction_date FROM sandbox.jg_banking_genie.client_interaction GROUP BY group_id)
SELECT t.group_id, t.group_name, t.segment, t.as_of_date, t.assets_at_bank_chf, l.last_interaction_date
FROM top100 t LEFT JOIN last_contact l ON l.group_id = t.group_id
WHERE l.last_interaction_date IS NULL OR l.last_interaction_date < add_months(current_date(), -6)
ORDER BY t.assets_at_bank_chf DESC

question: Asset allocation of the Steiner Family
sql:
WITH match AS (SELECT DISTINCT group_id FROM sandbox.jg_banking_genie.find_client('Steiner') WHERE group_name = 'Steiner Family'),
latest AS (SELECT max(as_of_date) AS d FROM sandbox.jg_banking_genie.position_monthly)
SELECT p.asset_class, p.as_of_date, round(sum(p.market_value_chf), 2) AS market_value_chf,
       round(sum(p.market_value_chf) / sum(sum(p.market_value_chf)) OVER (), 4) AS share_of_assets
FROM sandbox.jg_banking_genie.position_monthly p JOIN latest ON p.as_of_date = latest.d JOIN match m ON m.group_id = p.group_id
GROUP BY p.asset_class, p.as_of_date
ORDER BY market_value_chf DESC

content:
1. To identify a client, family or company by name, ALWAYS call sandbox.jg_banking_genie.find_client first, then filter by the returned group_id or party_id. Never use LIKE on names. find_client matches person and entity names, NOT group names: for a family or company such as "Meier Family" or "Steiner Family", call find_client with the core surname only (e.g. 'Meier'), never with the word "Family", and keep only the rows whose group_name equals the full group name. Group names are not unique, so if several groups (distinct group_id) are returned, list them all with group_id, group_name, segment and domicile_country and ask which one is meant. If none are returned, say the client was not found. Never guess.
2. "Net worth", "total wealth", "wealth with us", "total relationship" or "how much does X have" means the net position at the bank from v_group_net_position at the latest as_of_date. Always show assets at bank, liabilities at bank and net position at bank together, plus the as-of date. Show the KYC estimated total wealth separately, labelled "KYC-declared estimate of total wealth (not verified)". For a full overview of one client, use sandbox.jg_banking_genie.client_360.
3. When listing client groups, always include group_id, group_name, segment and domicile_country so users can tell same-named groups apart.
4. "Meet", "met" or "last meeting" refers only to in-person meetings: apply the "Meetings only" filter. When asked when we last met a client, also show the latest interaction across any channel as a separate column.
5. Only data held at the bank is available. Questions about external wealth (Forbes, other banks, public sources) must be answered with "not available in this data".
6. All amounts are in CHF. Use month-end snapshots; "current" means the latest as_of_date. Revenue periods default to the trailing 12 months.
7. A client group is the consolidated level (family or corporate group). A party is an individual or entity within it. Aggregate to group level unless the user asks about a person.
8. Apply the "Open accounts only" filter to account-based questions by default. For lending questions apply the "Lending accounts" filter, and use the "Credit utilisation" measure for utilisation.
